reasons: Classification is correct: Article XIII(b) caps only Licensor's liability at one half of amounts paid (well below six months' fees) and (a) excludes consequential damages only for Licensor, leaving Licensee uncapped — squarely in the rule's walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback of a mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs.

The redline is directionally right and actionable: it makes both the indirect-damages exclusion and the aggregate cap mutual, resets the basis to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the Excluded Claims carve-out sentence (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirms Licensee's payment obligations are not capped damages — i.e., the preferred position.

Edits are confined to the two operative sentences; paragraph (c) and the surrounding all-caps disclaimer language are untouched. The high changed-character ratio on sub-part (b) is expected because the cap basis and mutuality both had to be replaced, so it is not a substantive defect.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, states the playbook position and flags that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Minor, non-fatal notes for the negotiator: the added "EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS" qualifier now also opens the consequential-damages exclusion for Excluded Claims (including Licensee's indemnity obligations), which goes slightly beyond the model language's cap-only carve-out; and the residual Licensor-only IP-infringement disclaimer at the end of (a) remains inconsistent with the new mutual framing, though the rationale reasonably defers that to the IP indemnity rule.
